bug_semantics: A logged-in user could submit a saved graph configuration whose config_json was checked only for syntactically valid JSON. The server stored and returned the object without a property allowlist; an administrator's list included every user's saved configurations. Loading one parsed the stored JSON and applyConfig spread every property of attacker-controlled stixStyles or mispStyles entries into GRAPH_CONFIG. Those style maps were then passed to Pivotick as nodeStyleMap/defaultNodeStyle, and Pivotick interpreted a supplied svgIcon as HTML, so viewing/loading the saved configuration could execute attacker script in another user's browser.
flaw_origin: Commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a introduced the complete unsafe saved-configuration path in one focused feature commit: the graph_config model and save/list routes, unrestricted JSON persistence, the saved-config loader, and applyConfig's unrestricted style-object spreads. Its immediate parent had none of the graph-config persistence, loading, or patch-application mechanism, making this ordinary one-parent feature commit the smallest reconstructable BIC rather than the later branch merge or a release commit.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names author and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>, has the message 'add: [config] edit/create a json config for graph', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The first-party GitHub advisory API at https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-J8CV-PJX7-PVQF describes the chain: saved graph styles reach Pivotick, Pivotick interprets svgIcon as HTML, one user's configuration can be displayed to other users including administrators, and the remedy is a strict server/client schema plus sanitization of existing rows. It directly references fix commit 9b317587fa4ec11b6f72c2d1d8b98a686537b4fb.

git log -L 1401,1428:website/web/convert/convert.py a0a9834... attributes graph_config_list and graph_config_save to a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a. The introduced save route only called json.loads(config_json) and then save_graph_config(name, config_json, ...); the list route serialized stored config_json unchanged. The same commit's website/web/convert/convert_core.py get_graph_configs omitted any owner filter for administrators, exposing all active rows to them.

git log -L 533,552:website/web/static/js/graph/convertGraph.js a0a9834... attributes applyConfig to the BIC. Its stixStyles and mispStyles loops used {...existing, ...v}, admitting arbitrary properties such as svgIcon. In the same file, _initViewer passed the resulting styleMap to new window.Pivotick as render.nodeStyleMap and render.defaultNodeStyle.

git log -L 388,395:website/web/static/js/graph/graphConfigModal.js a0a9834... shows that this new file's _loadConfig parsed cfg.config_json and immediately called applyConfig(patch). The modal also offered a directly editable JSON tab and saved the resulting configuration through /convert/graph_config/save.

Direct immediate-parent tree verification used parent 11b0bc4583022cd863244af07040fcf5d9405738 from git cat-file -p a0a9834.... git cat-file -e 11b0bc4...:website/web/static/js/graph/graphConfigModal.js failed because the file did not exist, and git grep for graph_config|applyConfig|config_json across the parent versions of website/db_class/db.py, website/web/convert, website/web/static/js/graph, and website/web/templates/convert returned no matches. git diff --name-status parent..BIC shows the modal and migration added and the model, routes, core, graph renderer, and detail template changed together.

git cat-file -p a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a shows exactly one parent (11b0bc4583022cd863244af07040fcf5d9405738), author and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>, and no trailers or AI marker. The commit is therefore not a merge aggregate; no squash/member decomposition was indicated by the available commit topology.

Release-tree checks establish the boundary. git tag --contains a0a9834... returned v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5 but not v1.2; dereferenced tag commits are v1.2=8097afb2908eb292c30bfda94648631a781e38af, v1.3=ecd04d494b0fda2ab39fb56472785388c2d5872e, v1.4=bc46b6ed186786e672c1229d014a6d0a448fedad, and v1.5=fe093f9a1f9727068bc7e82ba47630907d859edb. git grep found no graph-config mechanism in v1.2; v1.3 and v1.4 retained the JSON-only save check, raw persistence, unrestricted style spreads, and applyConfig(patch).

git show 9b317587fa4ec11b6f72c2d1d8b98a686537b4fb is the direct one-parent fix: website/web/conversions/conversions.py validates clean JSON before saving and sanitizes stored config_json on list; conversions_core.py permits only known keys and only shape/color/size in style entries; conversionGraph.js calls sanitizeConfigPatch before merging; graphSafety.js independently filters the client patch and excludes svgIcon/iconClass. git tag --contains the fix returned only v1.5, and v1.5 tree grep confirms validate_graph_config, sanitize_stored_graph_config, and sanitizeConfigPatch while v1.4 still has the vulnerable path. Thus v1.3-v1.4 are affected releases and v1.5 is the first tagged fixed release.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a adds persistent graph configurations and accepts arbitrary JSON structure. A malicious authenticated user can place svgIcon inside a style entry, store it, and rely on an administrator's all-config listing to make that row available. The saved-config loader parses the row, applyConfig copies the unrecognized property into the live style map, and the renderer hands the map to Pivotick's HTML-interpreting svgIcon path. Line history identifies that feature commit itself, not the v1.3 merge that later carried it to a release. The immediate parent tree lacks every required graph-config source-to-sink component, directly proving parent absence. Tag ancestry and tag-tree content place the flaw first in v1.3, retain it in v1.4, and show the advisory's strict-schema fix first in v1.5. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: despite unrelated commits elsewhere in history, this BIC has a human author/committer and no AI marker. The closed causal verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
